# Results — Study 882 (Gas-Price → Discretionary, the "pump tax" rotation)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — a rise
in the **retail gasoline price** is a tax on the consumer's wallet, so a rising gas price
should forecast **consumer-discretionary (XLY) underperforming staples (XLP) next month**
and a **tailwind for energy (XLE)**; the predictive slope of the XLY−XLP forward one-month
spread on the trailing one-month gas return should be **negative**. Offline & deterministic
once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.
Stamped as-of 2026-06-30 (the last complete calendar month; the partial current month is dropped).
Fingerprint `c131f45ae347` (panel XLY close).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted close (`auto_adjust=True`, total-return), **RB=F** (front-month RBOB gasoline futures, the pump-price proxy) + **XLY** (discretionary) + **XLP** (staples) + **XLE** (energy) + **SPY** (market), 2005-01-03 → 2026-06-30, **5,412** aligned daily rows |
| Resample | month-end (`ME`) last close → monthly simple returns; **256** monthly observations (2005-02-28 → 2026-05-31) |
| Signal | the **trailing one-month gasoline (RB=F) return** known at the close of month `t` (the predictor `x`) |
| Target | the **forward one-month XLY−XLP spread return** over month `t+1` (`spread.shift(-1)`, the target `y`); a parallel run uses the energy tilt **XLE−SPY** |
| Regression | single-regressor OLS `y = α + β·x + ε`; the pump-tax slope `β` (forward spread return per unit monthly gas return), expected **< 0** |
| Execution / costs | one documented lag: gas return through close `t` → hold the spread over month `t+1`. The costed timer trades `−sign(gas_ret)` of the XLY−XLP spread (a 2× NAV long/short book), one-way cost × NAV per rebalance leg on both legs, 50 bps/yr borrow on the short leg |
| Statistics | Newey-West (HAC, 6-lag) *t* on the slope; OLS *t*; R²; a Welch tercile cross-check; a 2,000-permutation placebo; a two-era cut; a 20-seed synthetic positive control |

**Survivorship — named on the Signal axis.** RB=F, XLY, XLP, XLE and SPY are
continuously-listed liquid futures/ETFs, so there is **no delisting bias** on this basket;
the caveat is instead that **RB=F** is a front-month RBOB futures roll (with the usual roll /
seasonal-blend effects) used as a proxy for the *retail pump* price — a signal-construction
choice, not a survivorship one. (FRED weekly retail gasoline `GASREGW` is the textbook pump
series and would be an ideal confirmatory tape; FRED was unreachable from the build host, so
the traded RB=F price is the signal. RB=F and GASREGW co-move ≈0.9 monthly.)

## The headline — the predictive regression

`r_(XLY−XLP)[t+1] = α + β·r_gas[t]` on n = **256** months:

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| **slope β (pump-tax coefficient)** | **−0.0171** |
| Newey-West(6) *t* on β | **−0.71** |
| OLS *t* on β | −0.79 |
| R² | **0.25%** |
| α (intercept) | +0.26%/mo |
| fwd XLY−XLP after gas **fell** (bottom tercile) | +0.19% |
| fwd XLY−XLP after gas **rose** (top tercile) | −0.08% (Welch *t* = −0.40) |

The claimed edge **does not replicate.** The point estimate has the *right* (negative) sign
— gas up → discretionary lags staples next month — and even the tercile split leans the
predicted way (+0.19% after cheap gas vs −0.08% after dear gas). But the slope is
**−0.0171** with a Newey-West *t* of just **−0.71** and an R² of **0.25%**: statistically
indistinguishable from zero. The pump-tax rotation is directionally plausible and
economically a rounding error.

## The energy tilt — is dear gas at least a tailwind for XLE?

`r_(XLE−SPY)[t+1] = α + β·r_gas[t]` on the same 256 months (the claim expects **β > 0**):

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| slope β | **−0.0045** |
| Newey-West(6) *t* | **−0.11** |
| R² | **0.01%** |
| fwd XLE−SPY after gas **fell** | +0.21% |
| fwd XLE−SPY after gas **rose** | +0.56% (Welch *t* = +0.35) |

The regression slope is a flat zero (*t* = −0.11); the tercile split *does* lean the
predicted way (energy beats the market by +0.56% after dear-gas months vs +0.21% after
cheap-gas ones), but the Welch *t* on that gap is a non-significant +0.35. No forecastable
energy tailwind either — at best a whisper.

## Placebo — is the (tiny) slope even a lucky alignment?

Keep the predictor `x`, permute the target `y` (predictor → target link broken), 2,000 draws:

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| observed slope | **−0.0171** |
| placebo mean (sd) | +0.0004 (0.0218) |
| two-sided p (\|β\| ≥ observed) | **0.431** |

The observed slope sits comfortably inside the permutation null — p = 0.43, i.e. pure noise.
Nothing to explain.

## Robustness — two eras (split 2016-01-01), XLY−XLP target

| era | n | slope β | NW *t* | R² |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 2005-01 → 2016-01 | 131 | −0.0054 | −0.16 | 0.03% |
| 2016-01 → 2026-06 | 125 | −0.0289 | −0.88 | 0.57% |

The sign is at least *stable* (negative in both halves, unlike the crude→equity slope of
study 825 which flips) — but it stays firmly insignificant in both eras (|*t*| ≤ 0.88). A
consistently-signed nothing is still a nothing.

## The timer — can you get paid for it?

Trade `−sign(gas_ret[t])` of the XLY−XLP spread over month `t+1` (short the spread after gas
rises, long it after gas falls); the spread is a 2× NAV long/short book, one-way cost × NAV
per rebalance leg on both legs, 50 bps/yr borrow on the short leg.

| book | gross/mo | net/mo | *t* | Sharpe | ~ann. | hit |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| spread timer, 1 bp | +0.089% | +0.028% | +0.10 | 0.02 | +0.3% | 0.504 |
| spread timer, 5 bps | +0.089% | −0.046% | −0.16 | −0.04 | −0.5% | 0.504 |

A coin flip (hit rate 0.504): the gross edge is +0.089%/mo (*t* ≈ 0.3, not shown), and once
you pay realistic two-leg costs it is a flat-to-negative nothing. No paycheck. **Mirage.**

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic seeded daily tape where the XLY−XLP month-`t+1` return loads on the gas
month-`t` return with slope `−edge` (pump-tax direction) and the energy tilt loads `+edge`.
No network.

| world | slope NW *t* |
|---|--:|
| null (`edge = 0`), **20 seeds** | mean **−0.61** (sd 1.00), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 1/20 seeds** (≈ the nominal 5%; a 200-seed run centres at +0.05 with a 6% fire rate) |
| planted (`edge = 0.35`, seed 882) | β = **−0.1294**, ***t* = −5.92**, R² = 10.44% |

The regression recovers a *planted* negative pump-tax slope cleanly and fires on the null at
only the nominal rate — so the flat real-tape result is a genuine null, not a broken engine.
*(A faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The pump-tax rotation does **not** replicate on 2005–2026 US ETFs. The
  predictive slope of the XLY−XLP forward spread on the trailing gas return is **−0.0171**
  (Newey-West *t* = **−0.71**, R² = **0.25%**) — the *right* (negative) sign, but
  statistically indistinguishable from zero; p = 0.43 in a 2,000-draw placebo; insignificant
  and consistently tiny across both eras (*t* = −0.16 / −0.88). The energy tilt is flatter
  still (*t* = −0.11). A 20-seed synthetic control recovers a *planted* slope cleanly
  (*t* = −5.92), so the null is real. The story is directionally sensible and economically
  absent.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The spread timer is a coin flip (hit 0.504): gross +0.089%/mo,
  net **+0.028%/mo** at 1 bp and **−0.046%/mo** once you pay realistic two-leg costs, Sharpe
  ≈ 0. No paycheck here.
